does: Stirs raw orzo into a hot tomato sauce and stock, usually around braised meat, and bakes it uncovered in the oven until the pasta has taken up the liquid and is tender, with a slightly crisp top. The Greek name for the dish and its clay pot is giouvetsi.

intro.what: Raw orzo cooks in the oven in the sauce of the meat and takes it up as it swells.
intro.why: The pasta tastes of the sauce all the way through, and the whole meal comes out of one dish.

how: Have the meat and its sauce hot and the stock boiling.
Tip the sauce and the meat into a baking dish, stir in the raw orzo and pour in the hot stock.
Bake uncovered, stirring once halfway so that the grains on top do not dry out.
Take it out when the orzo is tender and most of the liquid is gone. It thickens as it stands.

cues.text: The liquid has sunk below the grains and the top has small golden patches.
A grain is soft right through with no chalky centre.

mistakes.mistake: Using cold stock, so that the orzo sits soaking and turns soft outside while the centre stays hard.
Too little liquid, so that the dish dries before the pasta is tender.
mistakes.fix: Keep a little hot stock or water to add halfway if it looks dry.

mistakes.mistake: Baking until no liquid is left at all, so that the dish turns stodgy as it stands.
mistakes.fix: Stop while it is still a little loose.

quiz.question: Why is the stock poured in hot?
choices: So that the orzo starts to cook at once and evenly.
quiz.because: Cold liquid leaves the pasta soaking before it cooks.

quiz.question: When does the dish come out of the oven?
choices: When the orzo is tender and a little loose liquid is left.
As soon as the top browns.
quiz.because: The pasta goes on taking up liquid as the dish stands.

variant_of.differs: The pasta goes into the dish raw with a hot sauce and stock and cooks in the oven by taking them up. It is not boiled first and baked after.
